description: Cys-axial b-type heme parameters covering ferric (Fe³⁺) and ferrous (Fe²⁺) states (cytochrome-P450-style heme with a single proximal thiolate ligand). Bonded parameters are derived from a QM Hessian of a small cluster optimized at a protein-context Cys backbone geometry. Heme + proximal Cys are split into two AMBER residues per state; the cross-residue Fe-Sγ bond is added by the transformer. (2026 rebuild: macrocycle H names regularized for the loadpdb path; macrocycle carbons forked CC/Cp/CD/CY/VB -> Ma/Mb/Mc/Md/Me (oxidized) / Mp-Mt with Mu/Mv pyrrole N (reduced) so the two redox states use disjoint atom-type sets and are mixed-redox-dimer safe; proximal-Cys redox response refit onto Sgamma. Value-neutral typing — bonded/vdW unchanged.)
references: Guberman-Pfeffer, M. J. Force field parameters for Cys-axial b-type hemes of the NOS oxygenase domain. Parameterization from PDB 2G6H substrate (L-Arg)-bound geometry; Yang 2016 HEB macrocycle + Seminario Fe-shell from B3LYP/[LANL2DZ+6-31G(d)] QM Hessian; Shahrokh 2012 IC6 Cys-axial-specific dihedrals.
Yang, L.; Capece, L.; Marti, M. A.; Estrin, D. A. AMBER force field parameters for the heme b prosthetic group of cytochrome P450 enzymes. Data in Brief 2016, 5, 99-104.

Shahrokh, K.; Orendt, A.; Yost, G. S.; Cheatham, T. E. Quantum mechanically derived AMBER-compatible heme parameters for various states of the cytochrome P450 catalytic cycle. J. Comput. Chem. 2012, 33 (2), 119-133.

Capece, L.; Lewis-Ballester, A.; Yeh, S.-R.; Estrin, D. A.; Marti, M. A. Complete reaction mechanism of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase as revealed by QM/MM simulations. J. Phys. Chem. B 2012, 116 (4), 1401-1413.

leaprc_groups.description: Constant-pH titratable protein residues (AS4/GL4 etc.) come from AMBER's constant-pH library.
The titratable PRN heme propionate is defined in AMBER's constant-redox library (conste.lib) - NOT in constph.lib. Constant-(pH,E) MD loads both together (the 'Constant pH + Redox' picker option).

oxidized.description: Ferric (Fe³⁺) heme — resting oxidized state. Sextet (S=5/2) high-spin in NOS substrate-bound geometry.

high_spin.description: High-spin Fe³⁺, S=5/2 sextet. Heme + Cys-thiolate sum to net 0e (Fe³⁺ + porph²⁻ + Cys⁻).

Guberman_HTO_RESP_constpH.description: Guberman-Pfeffer ferric Cys-axial b-type heme + proximal Cys thiolate, parameterized for NOS oxygenase domain (rat nNOS Cys415).
Guberman_HTO_RESP_constpH.reference: Yang 2016 HEB macrocycle + Seminario Fe-shell from B3LYP/[LANL2DZ+6-31G(d)] QM Hessian on the 2G6H substrate-bound model; Shahrokh 2012 IC6 Cys-axial dihedrals; Yang/Capece 2013 BBA Fe LJ.
Guberman_HTO_RESP_constpH.name: Ferric Cys-axial b-type heme + proximal Cys thiolate (HTO + CTO)
Guberman_HTO_RESP_constpH.methodology:
This is the Cys-axial b-type heme of the nitric-oxide synthase (NOS) oxygenase domain - cytochrome-P450-style, with a single proximal cysteine-thiolate ligand on iron - in its oxidized (ferric, Fe3+, high-spin S=5/2) state. The heme plus its proximal cysteine sum to a net charge of 0.

- Geometry: a small cluster (heme + the proximal cysteine, including the cysteine backbone) was optimized by DFT (B3LYP; LANL2DZ basis on iron, 6-31G(d) elsewhere) from the substrate-bound crystal structure (PDB 2G6H, rat nNOS with L-arginine bound), with the cysteine backbone angles frozen at the crystal values so the parameters reflect the real protein geometry rather than a gas-phase one.
- Bond and angle stiffness: the iron coordination shell (the Fe-N and Fe-S bonds and the angles around iron) is fit by the Seminario method, which reads these constants directly off the QM second-derivative matrix (the 'Hessian'); it is fit separately for the ferric and ferrous states. The rest of the porphyrin (macrocycle, vinyl, methyl groups) is taken from the published Yang (2016) heme-b parameters.
- Torsions around iron: from the published Shahrokh (2012) P450 Cys-axial set (transferable to NOS without re-fitting). Planarity (improper) terms from Yang 2016.
- Atomic charges: a two-stage RESP fit. The cysteine backbone atoms are pinned to their standard ff14SB cysteinate values so the residue splices cleanly into a protein; only the heme and the cysteine side chain are fit freely, with iron's charge constrained to its QM (Mulliken) value. Because the iron-sulfur bond is partly covalent, the heme and cysteine are allowed to carry fractional (non-integer) charges that sum to the correct whole number for the pair - capturing about half an electron of sulfur-to-iron donation (the sulfur ends up less negative, and iron less positive, than their textbook ionic values).
- Custom atom types: the macrocycle carbons are given short custom type names (Ma-Me (ferric)), together with a forked iron type (FO), so the two redox states use entirely separate type sets and can coexist in one topology (e.g. a mixed-oxidation-state multi-heme protein) without overwriting each other. This relabeling is value-neutral - it changes no charges or van der Waals (atom-size) values.

Caveat: the force constants are calibrated to the substrate-bound active site; for the empty (apo), NO-released, or six-coordinate (Fe-O2/NO/CO) states the iron-shell bonded model would need re-deriving. Iron's van der Waals parameters use the Yang/Capece (2013) values.

References: Yang 2016 (heme-b macrocycle); Shahrokh 2012 (P450 Cys-axial torsions); Seminario 1996 (Fe-shell constants from the QM Hessian); Bayly-Cieplak-Cornell-Kollman 1993 (two-stage RESP).

Guberman_HTO_RESP_FixedpH.name: Ferric Cys-axial b-type heme + proximal Cys thiolate (HTO + CTO)
Guberman_HTO_RESP_FixedpH.methodology:
This is the same ferric Cys-axial NOS heme parameter set as the constant-pH Guberman_HTO_RESP_constpH set - identical heme and proximal-Cys charges, bonded terms, and atom types - but with a 'fixed-pH' treatment of the two heme propionates. The default set represents each propionate with the titratable PRN residue, whose library lives in AMBER's constant-pH framework (leaprc.constph); loading it forces the whole protein onto the older parm10/ff10 backbone and loses ff14SB/ff19SB refinements. This fixed-pH set instead bundles two static propionate residues directly in the heme library: PRD (deprotonated carboxylate, COO-, net -1) and PRP (protonated carboxylic acid, COOH, net 0, syn conformer). You pick each ring's protonation state independently at build time (A-ring and D-ring), and the system loads cleanly under a modern protein force field (ff14SB or ff19SB) with no constant-pH dependency.

- Propionate charges are taken verbatim from parmed's titratable_residues PRN definition (state 0 -> PRD, state 1 -> PRP); the four inactive 'ghost' hydroxyl hydrogens of the constph PRN are dropped exactly, since they carry zero charge and zero van der Waals radius. PRD has 9 atoms (net -1), PRP has 10 (net 0).
- All propionate atom types are standard parm10 (identical to ASP/GLU/ASH/GLH), so their bonded terms come from the base force field and no propionate-specific frcmod entries are needed. The frcmod is otherwise identical to the default set's.
- The heme (HTO) and proximal Cys (CTO) units, their charges, bonded terms, custom atom types, and the cross-residue Fe-S and propionate attachment bonds are unchanged from the default set.

Net charge (heme + Cys + A-ring + D-ring) for ferric (Fe3+, S=5/2): -2 / -1 / 0 for (PRD,PRD) / one-protonated / (PRP,PRP).

Use this set when you are NOT running constant-pH MD on the propionates and want the protein to keep ff14SB/ff19SB refinements. For constant-pH MD on the propionates, use the constant-pH Guberman_HTO_RESP_constpH set instead.

reduced.description: Ferrous (Fe²⁺) heme — one-electron reduced state. Quintet (S=2) high-spin in NOS substrate-bound geometry.

high_spin.description: High-spin Fe²⁺, S=2 quintet. Heme + Cys-thiolate sum to net -1e (Fe²⁺ + porph²⁻ + Cys⁻). Tleap emits one expected 'unit charge -1.0 is not zero' warning.

transforms_from: HEM residue in the input PDB (b-type heme; standard PDB ligand code)
Single CYS residue whose SG is within 2.5 Å of the heme Fe (the proximal Cys; e.g., Cys415 in rat nNOS)
creates_bonds: Two inter-residue propionate attachment bonds at C2A and C3D (HTO/HTR.C2A - PRN_A.CA, HTO/HTR.C3D - PRN_D.CA). The bare β-carbons C2A and C3D are sp2 CB atoms in the lib — no methyl-cap CT carbons.
transformation_info.notes: Both HEM and the proximal CYS are renamed by the transformer (HEM->HTO/HTR, CYS->CTO/CTR). The heme's two propionate side chains are extracted as PRN residues (constant-pH library, leaprc.constph) and re-attached to the macrocycle at C2A and C3D — DIFFERENT from the legacy NOS parameterization which used methyl-cap CAA/CAD attachment points. Cys-axial dihedrals (X-Fe-SH-X, CC-NP-FE-SH, CD-NO-FE-SH, CC-NP-FE-NP, CD-NO-FE-NO) are taken verbatim from Shahrokh 2012 IC6 (published P450 Cys-axial values, valid for NOS without re-fitting); the macrocycle bonded terms are from Yang 2016 HEB; only the state-specific Fe-shell bonds and angles are re-fit per redox state.

methodology:
Cluster model: small model truncates the heme + proximal Cys (full Cys including N/H/CA/HA/CB/HB2/HB3/SG/C/O backbone) for Seminario bonded-parameter input. The QM model intentionally excludes heme propionate atoms (CAA/CBA/CGA/O1A/O2A on pyrrole A and CAD/CBD/CGD/O1D/O2D on pyrrole D) and replaces them with H atoms on the pyrrole β-carbons C2A and C3D during ESP/RESP. Cap-Hs constrained to charge zero in the RESP fit and dropped from the final lib, leaving C2A and C3D as bare sp2 CB atoms ready for cross-residue bonds to PRN.

DFT method: B3LYP / LANL2DZ (Fe) + 6-31G(d) (light atoms). Modredundant-frozen Cys phi and psi during geometry optimization at the rat nNOS·CaM-bound crystal values, preventing the capped Cys dipeptide from relaxing to a gas-phase Ramachandran-favored geometry that doesn't reflect the protein context.

Bonded parameters from Seminario on the diagonal blocks of the Cartesian Hessian. Per-state ferric/ferrous parameters re-fit for: Fe-NP, Fe-NO, Fe-SH bonds; NP-Fe-NO (cis), NP-Fe-NP (trans), NO-Fe-NO (trans), NP-Fe-SH, NO-Fe-SH, Fe-SH-Cβ, Fe-NP-Cα, Fe-NO-Cα angles. All other bonded terms (macrocycle backbone, vinyl, methyl, propionate junctions) inherited verbatim from Yang 2016 HEB; Cys-axial-specific dihedrals inherited verbatim from Shahrokh 2012 IC6.

RESP charges: 2-stage Bayly-Cieplak-Cornell-Kollman procedure. Stage 1 constraints: ff14SB CYM backbone charges fixed (N, H, CA, HA, C, O — so the production CYM backbone splices into the protein at canonical values); Fe Mulliken constrained per state (+0.7324 ferric, +0.5258 ferrous). Stage 1 free fit: Cys CB/HB2/HB3/SG, heme heavy atoms + 28 H. Stage 2 equivalences: methyl-H trios averaged, methylene-H pairs averaged.

Fe-S covalency captured: residue-level integer-charge requirement intentionally relaxed (heme alone = +0.326 ferric / -0.406 ferrous; Cys alone = -0.326 ferric / -0.594 ferrous), so the complex sums to the integer formal charge (0 ferric / -1 ferrous) but each residue carries fractional charge representing ~0.5 e of S→Fe donation. RESP picks up that the Cys-SG charge is less negative than canonical CYM thiolate (-0.88 e in ff14SB), and the Fe charge is correspondingly less positive than the formal +3 / +2.

Validation: tleap build of isolated combine{HTO CTO} + explicit Fe-Sγ bond reports 'Unit is OK' with all parameters resolved; ferrous reports the one expected unit-charge warning. Mixed-state combine{HTO CTO HTR CTR} also clean (FO/FR atom-type fork prevents cross-state clobbering).
